summary: Step 2 (FOUNDATION) DONE. SQLite source-of-truth schema, versioned migrations, repository ports and restart-recovery tests. ports/repositories.py defines 8 structural typing.Protocol ports (Project/Step/Task/ArchitectureVersion/ADR/Risk/Finding/Decision) plus TaskKey(step_no, attempt); the domain Task stays untouched (no id field) because (step_no, attempt) is the identity. infrastructure/repositories.py provides 8 SEPARATE concrete adapters (SqliteProjectRepository, SqliteStepRepository, SqliteTaskRepository, SqliteArchitectureVersionRepository, SqliteADRRepository, SqliteRiskRepository, SqliteFindingRepository, SqliteDecisionRepository) - not one catch-all class - each with its own key/type contract, sharing one sqlite3.Connection and private helpers. All writes use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(<key>) DO UPDATE SET ... (never INSERT OR REPLACE); this is proven by tests asserting stable row identity for tasks and by a test showing a step upsert with a dependent task would violate the FK under REPLACE. Schema is column-per-field (enums as TEXT, datetimes as ISO-8601 TEXT, bool as INTEGER 0/1, sequences as JSON arrays, mappings as JSON objects) with the single semantically guaranteed foreign key tasks.step_no -> steps.step_no plus UNIQUE(step_no, attempt); PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON is enforced on every connection. Migrations: schema_migrations is the bootstrap table (version INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name, applied_at), the ordered MIGRATIONS tuple is validated for uniqueness/order, and each migration runs atomically via explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK so a failing migration is rolled back (partial DDL removed) and never marked as applied. open_database(path) resolves and creates data/architecture_assistant.db by default (path injectable; tests use :memory: or tmp_path); .mini_build/ was not touched. sqlite3 is imported only inside infrastructure/ - domain/ and ports/ contain no persistence code. Scope respected: no API, no UI, no plugins, no loop. 105 new tests (16 migration + 89 repository) on top of Step 1, all deterministic ordering asserted (ORDER BY primary key).
